correctness.rationale: The full spectrum is true. In frozen RESULT.md lines 21–55, reducing the powers of b modulo b^r+1 gives signed residue-class digit counts c_i. When the total digit weight is at most b, the integer signed evaluation has absolute value at most b*b^(r-1)=b^r, strictly less than the modulus. It must be zero; a coefficient of magnitude b would use all the weight with no other coefficient to cancel it. All remaining coefficients have magnitude less than b, so successive reductions modulo b give c_i=0 for every i, forcing even weight. The b+1 witness uses distinct positions because r>=2 and evaluates to 1+b*b^(r-1) modulo the modulus; the modulus itself has digit sum 2. Disjoint digit blocks add sums without carries. These two generators and the short-weight obstruction give the spectrum, count, largest gap and density, also for b=2. Inspected the frozen verification notes/code without execution; an independent bounded modular replay checked the b+1 witness for 60 pairs (even b=2 through 20, r=2 through 7). The frozen reachability checker, if run, covers all numeral lengths only for its tested parameters and digit caps, not the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The whole spectrum is a direct block-base corollary of established digit-sum facts. Set B=b^r and suppose N is a positive multiple of B+1 with s_b(N)<=b. For t=0,...,r-1, regroup the base-b digits of b^t N in blocks of r: s_B(b^t N)<=b^(r-1)s_b(N)<=B. Each b^t N is still a multiple of B+1. In even base B, no multiple of B+1 has odd digit sum at most B: by Clokie et al. Theorem 3, such a sum would be a signed sum of that many ±1 terms divisible by B+1, impossible. Since b is even, the parity of s_B(b^t N) is the sum of the digits of N in positions j with j+t congruent to 0 mod r. Each residue-class sum is therefore even and so is s_b(N). This handles even and odd r, not just the divisor-inclusion case. For sufficiency, the known digit-sum increment Theorem 4 applied to the sum 2 of the modulus gives b+1, and no-carry block concatenation gives precisely the proposed semigroup. This is positive coverage by reduction to prior results, not a failure for lack of access or an inference from same-day priority.
